brief.ask: Create a brand identity for Quorvo, the meeting assistant in this folder.
brief.owner: Owner preferences: calm, competent and human; for remote teams who are tired of meetings. No sparkles, stars, brains, robots, chat bubbles, waveforms or gradient blobs. Web app, a desktop app icon (macOS, Windows) and social.

claim.notes: Only knot passed the gate (narrowly, with a recurring question-mark reading) after two rounds; it was finalized with an accepted insufficient-evidence originality risk, and the Quorvo/Qorvo name conflict needs legal review.

concepts.title: Circled
readsAs: the word quorvo with two hand-circled clay o's
a refresh/reload arrow glyph in each o
the icon reads VO / v0 (Vercel's AI product) - unfortunate: a loading or retry spinner
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a spiral / swirl, snail shell or loading spinner; s2 an enso brush circle (zen cliche, stock-shape 0.74); s3 a plain lowercase q in a rounded sans, generic and would collide with knot's q; s4 'vo' with the o as an open pen loop: the end of the word, the circling gesture inside it; s5 a circled V, the vegan label. Struck s1 (spiral), s2 (enso), s3 (stock q, too close to knot), s5 (vegan mark). Pick s4 because the concept is wordmark-led: the circle earns its place inside 'quorvo' as the final o, not as a standalone icon. Development move: set the whole word in a calm humanist lowercase and draw only the final o as the hand-made circling stroke, closing nearly shut with a small overshoot so it reads as o first, gesture second; the icon then is that loop cropped from the word, tested hard against spiral/@/spinner readings. Do not reintroduce a q; that is knot's territory.

concepts.title: Handoff
readsAs: a lowercase n fused to a v (the letters rv, or a stylised N)
Greek nu / an N monogram for a brand starting with N
a stock geometric-sans wordmark with one ligature - unfortunate: 'RV' or an N-brand, i.e. the icon names a letter that is not in the brand's initial
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a stock flat-roof rv ligature, invisible in the word below 64 px (generic, not ownable); s2 an r whose arm turns down into the v in one stroke, the only sketch where a stranger sees a single continuous gesture; s3 a crude overlap, rv collides into an lv/N shape (struck); s4 the swollen arc makes rv read as an n with an angled leg, so the word reads quonvo at 16-32 px (struck, different letter). Pick s2, conditionally: in compare.png the word still reads as a stock geometric sans with a barely-there join, about 5 on distinctiveness and memorability. The one move: make the r-to-v turn the single signature gesture of the word, drawn as a visibly hand-made, slightly heavier continuous stroke with a clear notch where the r arm meets the v so it never closes into an n, and carry that same curve quality into o, u, q so the word stops looking like a default sans. Risk: a bare rv icon reads as RV (camper); the icon must be the joined stroke itself, not the two letters.

concepts.title: Knot
readsAs: a lowercase q drawn as a looped cord with the stem passing under
a shepherd's crook or cane with a curled tail
a rotated question mark or a 9 (unfortunate: at 16 px a smudged '?' or pig's-tail squiggle)
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 two stacked glyphs, an 'a' over a script hook (Bengali/Devanagari-like), 16px a blot; s2 'a' stacked on a 'G'/'6', two letters not one q; s3 'q' over 'p', a ligature 'qp'; s4 one loop whose stroke crosses its stem and flicks out: a looped q / script letter, the only one where the string IS the letter. Struck s1-s3: the knot hangs below as a second letter, so the word-level read is two characters. Keep s4. Risks: at 16px it reads as a script glyph (ơ / Bengali vowel) or a pin, and the knot is only a cross, not a tie. Development move: make the crossing read as string over string (visible over/under gap, slight hand-made taper, loose end with a soft curl) and keep the bowl generous and open so it stays a calm q, not a foreign letterform. Keep away from circled's open pen loop: knot owns the crossing, not the circling.

concepts.title: Pushed in
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s6 a hat brim with a crown, or a sunrise over a sagging horizon; 16 px a dash with a dot. s7 a bump in a line: a pulse/waveform blip or a speed bump (brief bans waveforms); 16 px a tilde. s8 a hat (bowler/sombrero) or sun on a horizon; 16 px same. s9 an eyebrow over a closed eye / sleepy emoji face, two rounded bars (brief bans pills echoing note lines). No sketch reads as a table or a chair; the chair-from-behind idea needs a viewpoint the stranger never takes, so a rework of the same move will keep reading as hat, sunrise or face. Different move: drop the furniture metaphor; find a form whose first reading is itself (e.g. a hand-made enclosure or a handed-over object) rather than a scene that needs a caption.
